canonical_task: linear-time unification (Paterson-Wegman)
citation: Paterson & Wegman, Linear unification, JCSS 16 (1978)

canonical_task: closure computation, poly-time
citation: Jones & Laaser, Complete problems for deterministic polynomial time, TCS 3 (1976)

canonical_task: simulate t steps, poly-time in (t, size)
citation: GHR (1995); Berlekamp, Conway & Guy, Winning Ways (Game of Life universality)

canonical_task: sweepline triangulation, poly-time
citation: Atallah, Callahan & Goodrich, P-complete geometric problems, Int. J. Comput. Geom. Appl. 3 (1993)

canonical_task: single-unit deadlock detection is P-complete (log-space complete for P)
citation: Spirakis (1986); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: simple-type typability is P-complete (log-space equiv. to unification; full ML let-polymorphism is DEXPTIME)
citation: Dwork-Kanellakis-Mitchell (1984); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: Path System Accessibility is P-complete
citation: Cook, An observation on time-storage trade-off, STOC 1973 / JCSS 9 (1974) [Path System Accessibility: first P-complete problem]; catalogued in Greenlaw-Hoover-Ruzzo (1995)
note: Cook's original P-complete problem (1974); the historic anchor of P-completeness theory (GHR 1995)

canonical_task: b-Chromatic Number decision: b(G) >= k?
citation: Irving & Manlove, The b-chromatic number of a graph, Discrete Appl. Math. 91 (1999) 127-141
note: computing b(G) is NP-hard (Irving-Manlove 1999); NP-complete even for connected bipartite graphs (deciding b(G)=Delta+1)

canonical_task: Capacitated Dominating Set decision: a capacitated dominating set of size <= k?
citation: generalizes Dominating Set (Karp 1972; Garey & Johnson 1979 [GT2]) — set all capacities to n
note: NP-complete (contains ordinary Dominating Set as the uncapacitated case). Distinct from ordinary/​connected dominating set (S2)

canonical_task: Connectivity Augmentation decision: <= t links raising edge-connectivity to k+1?
citation: Frederickson & Jaja, Approximation algorithms for several graph augmentation problems, SIAM J. Comput. 10 (1981) 270-283
note: NP-hard even unweighted on trees of diameter 4 (Frederickson-Jaja 1981). Distinct from vertex-connectivity augmentation and from unweighted edge-connectivity increase without a link set (poly-time, Wa

canonical_task: Efficient Domination decision: does G have a perfect code?
citation: Bange, Barkauskas & Slater, Efficient dominating sets in graphs (1988); NP-completeness also via Kratochvil
note: NP-complete — not every graph has a perfect code, so this is an existence/feasibility problem. Distinct from ordinary Dominating Set (S2)

canonical_task: 2D bin packing decision: pack into <= k unit bins? NP-complete (contains 1D bin packing = PARTITION)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: 1D bin packing (a restriction) is NP-complete via PARTITION

canonical_task: Grundy Number decision: Gamma(G) >= k? NP-complete
citation: Bonnet, Foucaud, Kim & Sikora, Complexity of Grundy coloring and its variants, Discrete Applied Mathematics 262 (2019) 65-77

canonical_task: Label Cover decision (exists a total labelling satisfying all edges): NP-complete (generalizes graph colouring / 2-CSP)
citation: Dinur & Safra, On the hardness of approximating label-cover, Information Processing Letters 89 (2004) 247-254
note: the projection-game / PCP backbone; exact feasibility is an NP-complete CSP

canonical_task: MAX-FLS decision: a feasible subsystem of size >= k? NP-complete
citation: Amaldi & Kann, The complexity and approximability of finding maximum feasible subsystems of linear relations, Theoretical Computer Science 147 (1995) 181-210
note: NP-hard (cf. Johnson & Preparata, The densest hemisphere problem, TCS 6 (1978) 93-107)

canonical_task: MinLA decision: a linear arrangement of total edge length <= B?
citation: Garey, Johnson & Stockmeyer, Some simplified NP-complete graph problems, TCS 1 (1976) 237-267

canonical_task: Minimum Equivalent Digraph decision: a reachability-preserving subgraph with <= k arcs?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Minimum Equivalent Digraph, GT34]
note: NP-complete; generalizes Hamiltonian Cycle on strongly connected digraphs

canonical_task: Mixed Postman decision: a closed traversal walk of length <= L?
citation: Papadimitriou, On the complexity of edge traversing, JACM 23 (1976) 544-554
note: NP-complete on mixed graphs (poly for all-undirected or all-directed)

canonical_task: Pathwidth decision: pathwidth <= k?
citation: Kashiwabara & Fujisawa, NP-completeness of the problem of finding a minimum-clique-number interval graph containing a given graph, Proc. ISCAS 1979, 657-660
note: NP-complete (via interval-graph completion / vertex separation); cf. Arnborg, Corneil & Proskurowski, SIAM J. Algebraic Discrete Methods 8 (1987) 277-284 for treewidth

canonical_task: Quadratic Congruences: exists z<=c with z^2≡a (mod b)?
citation: Manders & Adleman, NP-complete decision problems for binary quadratics, JCSS 16 (1978) 168-184
note: reduction from 3-SAT; one of the few number-theoretic NP-complete problems not known to be in NP∩coNP

canonical_task: Resource-constrained scheduling decision: schedule within makespan T?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Complexity results for multiprocessor scheduling under resource constraints, SIAM J. Comput. 4 (1975) 397-411
note: NP-complete even with a single resource

canonical_task: Sparsest Cut decision: a cut of ratio <= r?
citation: Matula & Shahrokhi, Sparsest cuts and bottlenecks in graphs, Discrete Appl. Math. 27 (1990) 113-123

canonical_task: Thickness decision: does G have thickness <= 2?
citation: Mansfield, Determining the thickness of graphs is NP-hard, Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 93 (1983) 9-23
note: NP-complete already for thickness two (reduction from Planar-3SAT)

canonical_task: Upper Domination decision: a minimal dominating set of size >= k?
citation: Bazgan et al., The many facets of upper domination, Theoretical Computer Science 717 (2018) 2-25

canonical_task: Eulerian-orientation existence: exists iff every vertex has even degree — orient the edges along an Euler tour; a poly (indeed trivial) decoupling witness
citation: Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis, Comment. Acad. Sci. Petropol. 8 (1736) 128-140
note: even-degree characterization underlies existence; an Euler tour yields an Eulerian orientation in linear time

canonical_task: DNF satisfiability is trivially in P (a DNF is satisfiable unless every term is contradictory)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: the decision version is easy -> a decoupling witness against the hard counting version
